correctness.rationale: Pinned random-walk equilibrium is unique by lambda-contraction. Exact two-boundary gap Green function gives support cx+(1-cx)p; the hub consistency equation solves to positive-denominator X, with gap minima at farthest midpoints. Strict discrete concavity of q_m and strict monotonicity of X in Q show precisely balanced hub-free placements, with label counts via rooted gap compositions; the hub-included branch is exactly a maximum-gap minimization. Rational direct equilibrium computations corroborate all subsets on n=4..8 and the exact rational hub-free example.

originality.rationale: Relevant full primary manuscripts and published mathematical records were compared for mathematical implication. Allagan et al. introduce the discounted hitting support and solve spiders/stars and degree-two gap problems, but their wheel-free results do not imply the global hub self-consistency or strict balanced-optimum classification for a degree-three rim. Closest known published database result solves complete bipartite graphs, not wheels. Relevant group hitting-probability algorithms concern query ranking rather than minimum worst-support wheel placement. Priority remains provisional against unindexed or unread sources.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be certified against unindexed or inaccessible equivalent wheel work.

value.rationale: The natural first cyclic graph with a universal hub has nontrivial global interactions between rim source gaps. Complete exact maximin characterizations and enumerations for every cardinality and arbitrary discount replace exponential search; the smallest wheel gives a sharp center-exclusion effect. The result bridges the generic NP-hard model and tree-only exact algorithms, and supplies exact optimizer multiplicities beyond scalar thresholds.
